transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 50 minutes today so we'll focus on the renewal and the expansion asks - quick intro?
[00:07] Rajiv Menon: Yeah hi, Rajiv here. Thanks, Ethan. We have Sophie and Tom on. Appreciate you making time.
[00:12] Sophie Laurent: Hey all.
[00:13] Tom Reyes: Tom here.
[00:15] Lila Gomez: Hi, Lila from Redwood, I'll jump into the perf stuff and the benchmarks.
[00:20] Ethan Chen: Cool. Quick agenda - confirm Peregrine's regions and QPS, walk through Dedicated options and pricing, security / compliance caveats, and then next steps. Sound good?
[00:29] Rajiv Menon: Yep. To summarize stance - we're renewing in June, want to expand to EU-west and APAC by Q3, and we need predictable latency SLAs for our 2nd line customer facing routing. Also curious about data residency and encryption.
[00:42] Ethan Chen: Got it. Sophie, can you speak to the traffic patterns and QPS?
[00:46] Sophie Laurent: Sure. Right now US-east is about 450 qps during peak for our inference calls. Typical sequence length is 512 tokens average, peaks at 1,024. EU traffic is lower now but projected to grow to 200 qps after we launch localized marketing. APAC is new - estimate 150 qps first 3 months. We also prioritize p95 latency under 200 ms.
[01:10] Lila Gomez: Okay that's helpful. A couple of immediate notes - Dedicated Reserved pools will give you predictability on throughput; we can size to match your p95 target depending on model and quant profile. One caveat, if you push quant too aggressively you might see a small bump in latency variance, tradeoff for cost.
[01:28] Rajiv Menon: Can you remind us of the difference between burst capacity and reserved capacity? Last time the docs got a bit fuzzy for our infra team.
[01:35] Ethan Chen: Yeah totally. Reserved is the committed pool for your account - consistent GPUs pinned to you. Burst is temporary extra capacity we can route to during spikes, but it's not SLA-backed for latency; reserved has the SLA. We'll include tiers in the quote.
[01:48] Tom Reyes: From procurement perspective, budget constraints mean we may start with 2 regions reserved and add the 3rd as a burst or on-demand, if pricing looks right.
[01:57] Lila Gomez: That's a common pattern. For EU-west, if you need strict data residency we can deploy a Private control plane in that region or enable regional tenancy with KMS key scoped to that region. There are slight ops differences, arguable more paperwork for private/on-prem.
[02:12] Sophie Laurent: On encryption - we need CMEK and audit logs for model inputs retained for 30 days for debugging. Is that supported?
[02:19] Ethan Chen: Yes, CMEK is supported on Dedicated and Private. Audit logs are available - we'll include sample retention options. Note that retaining full inputs may trigger additional compliance review, but technically supported.
[02:31] Rajiv Menon: Also curious on performance - last PoC we did, the KV cache seemed to be a big win for prefix-heavy workloads. Any new recommendations?
[02:39] Lila Gomez: Absolutely. The KV-cache improvements we've shipped last quarter cut token generation work for repeated prefixes by about 40% in our internal tests. For your workload with repeated routing prompts, enabling auto-prefix caching plus a small context window delta reduces both latency and cost. I'll share a spreadsheet with per-model numbers.
[02:57] Ethan Chen: Great, can you drop that link?
[02:59] Lila Gomez: I'll share it after the call - s3 link in the notes.
[03:02] [small crosstalk]
[03:10] Tom Reyes: On procurement timeline - if we want to lock pricing ahead of June renewal, when do we need a signed amendment?
[03:16] Ethan Chen: We usually need signed amendment 30 days before the renewal to avoid proration weirdness. So by end of May ideally, or we can do a mid-April commitment to reserve capacity.
[03:25] Rajiv Menon: Understood. One more technical thing - region-to-region replication for KV cache or stateful routing, is that supported?
[03:33] Lila Gomez: We don't replicate KV cache across regions because latency and consistency get tricky; instead we suggest per-region caches and warm-up strategies, plus cross-region fallbacks. If you want global state, that's more of an architecture piece we can consult on - there are patterns.
[03:46] Sophie Laurent: Are there any vendor lock-in concerns with model-specific kernels or quant profiles? We run some models in-house and want freedom to move.
[03:54] Lila Gomez: Good question. Our runtime has optimizations per architecture, but models export and run with standard weights; quant profiles are reversible in most cases. We'll provide recommended quant configs but you can keep source model artifacts. We avoid opaque formats.
[04:10] Ethan Chen: Let's talk pricing options - we can do a 12-month renewal with committed Reserved capacity for two regions and optional 3rd region on burst. Adding a 3-region Dedicated bundle reduces per-token cost by approx 18% vs two region baseline. I'll follow up with an itemized quote.
[04:27] Tom Reyes: Do you offer monthly or annual billing for Dedicated?
[04:30] Ethan Chen: Both. Annual commitment gives better unit economics and higher SLA priority. Monthly is available as rolling reserved capacity but pricing is slightly higher.
[04:38] Rajiv Menon: For the SLA, we need p95 latency SLA of 220 ms for core routing - will Redwood include credits or penalties?
[04:47] Ethan Chen: Yes, SLA credits are part of the Dedicated enterprise package. We'll include an SLA addendum showing uptime and latency commitments and credit tiers.
[04:55] Sophie Laurent: Any known degradation modes? We want graceful fallback if a region is constrained.
[04:59] Lila Gomez: We support smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants in other regions or lower tier models; you can set policy to prefer latency or cost. Also can set canary rollouts for model updates.
[05:12] Rajiv Menon: Ok thanks. A security item - we require a SOC2 report and a pen test attestation. Do you have recent reports?
[05:19] Ethan Chen: Yes, SOC 2 Type II is available - link in the notes. We also provide pen test summary reports and can set up an NDA to share full results.
[05:27] Tom Reyes: For procurement, can you provide a sample SOW for Dedicated setup and any migration support?
[05:33] Ethan Chen: Yep. We'll include a sample SOW and onboarding timeline in the follow-up. Usually onboarding is 4-6 weeks for Dedicated with network, KMS, and infra provisioning.
[05:44] [pause]
[05:47] Sophie Laurent: On the tuning side, can Lila outline what the benchmark sheet will contain?
[05:51] Lila Gomez: Sure - per-model latency at p50/p95, token cost, memory footprint, recommended quant profile (8-bit/4-bit where safe), KV-cache hit improvements, and recommended batching settings given your QPS and seq length. Also a checklist for region provisioning steps.
[06:08] Rajiv Menon: For APAC rollout, we may need a private control plane due to customer data agreements. What's the delta in cost and timeline?
[06:16] Lila Gomez: Private control plane adds a setup cost and a small monthly platform fee. Timeline usually 6-8 weeks. We'll include a ballpark delta in the quote; placement depends on whether you want on-prem or VPC-hosted private plane.
[06:29] Ethan Chen: Quick recap: Redwood items - pricing for 3-region Dedicated, SLA addendum, benchmark spreadsheet, sample SOW, security docs. Peregrine items - confirm final QPS by region and procurement timeline.
[06:41] Tom Reyes: We'll try to confirm procurement steps by Wednesday next week.
[06:44] Sophie Laurent: I'll pull exact QPS numbers and some traffic traces for the perf team.
[06:49] Rajiv Menon: Also please include in the quote the option to convert burst to reserved mid-term without major penalties.
[06:56] Ethan Chen: We can make that work; detail in the contract.
[06:59] [small talk]
[07:03] Ethan Chen: Anything else?
[07:05] Sophie Laurent: One last thing - can Redwood run a 24-hour soak test in EU-west once reserved is provisioned? We want to see steady-state thermal behavior.
[07:13] Lila Gomez: Yes we can run a soak with synthetic traffic; I'll list the parameters in the benchmark doc.
[07:19] Rajiv Menon: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[07:22] Ethan Chen: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the materials by end of week.
[07:25] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache), speaker overlaps, and truncated punctuation as typical with auto transcripts.
